To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction of laser radiation with chemically active systems is a complex phenomenon that is determined by the competition of various physical and chemical processes, and that the results of the interaction of laser beams with chemically active gases are strongly dependent on the initial conditions.

the interaction of a laser beam with a gas medium containing a fast chemical reaction can result in the appearance of a new type of nonlinear effect, namely, a nonlinear chemical effect, which can be characterized as the formation of a "chemical lens" in the medium.

laser irradiation of gas mixtures containing a fast-reacting component leads to strong nonuniform heating and to the formation of a temperature field that is inhomogeneous on a scale comparable with the optical length of the laser beam.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of the thermokinetic processes induced in a chemically active gageous medium by laser radiation.
the study of thermokinetic processes induced in chemically active media by laser radiation.
the study of the interaction of chemical kinetics and laser radiation, which is of great importance in the development of new methods of laser processing of materials and in laser chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the laser radiation is capable of inducing a wide variety of thermokinetic processes in chemically active media.
the laser beam in a chemical medium is an efficient tool for the control of chemical reactions.
, in general, the laser beam is a powerful tool to control chemical reactions in gaseous media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the laser-induced processes in chemically active media are of great interest and importance for the solution of many problems in the physics and chemistry of gaseous media, and in laser technology.
we observed and studied some new phenomena of chemical kinetics and nonlinear optics.
laser radiation is an efficient means for controlling the chemical composition of a gas mixture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chemical nonlinearity is an important factor in the formation of temperature fields and concentration profiles of the components during laser irradiation of chemically active gasses.
laser radiation can be used to create a variety of chemical and physical processes in chemically active media.
a chemically active gas mixture, in which a chemical reaction takes place, can be considered as a nonlinear optical medium.
